title: Shared judgments of moral decline can coexist with disagreement over whether government should promote values
source_unit: Gallup May 2026 Values and Beliefs poll and moral-values survey
geography: United States; national adults, party groups, and religious-attendance groups

observations.period: May 1-17, 2026; Gallup values and beliefs field period

denominator.unit: U.S. adults in the moral-values telephone survey; question-specific bases vary

moral_values_rating.unit: percent rating U.S. moral values as poor

moral_values_direction.unit: percent saying moral values are getting worse

perceived_government_influence.unit: percent saying government policies significantly affect moral values

government_should_promote_values.unit: percent saying government should promote moral values; 50% say it should not

cultural_judgment.value: Issue-specific moral acceptability remains selective and divided across party and religious-attendance groups rather than moving as one uniform national culture score

mechanism.value: A shared perception of moral decline can coexist with disagreement over government legitimacy, because recognizing institutional influence is not the same as granting the institution a legitimate role

observations.method: Structured extraction from Gallup's published survey estimates of moral-value ratings, perceived change, government influence and role, religious influence, and issue-specific moral acceptability; aggregate judgments are kept separate from observed conduct and policy effects.
observations.uncertainty: This is cross-sectional self-reported opinion. It does not retain respondent-level policy exposure, media or source environment, prior identity, local institutional encounter, personal conduct, policy implementation, political action, trust change, or later behavior.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults with question-specific party, religious-attendance, and issue subgroups; subgroup bases and margins are not reproduced here.
observations.counterinterpretation: Broad agreement that values are worsening may reflect national discourse or identity rather than an objective moral decline, while support or opposition to a government role may reflect long-standing ideology rather than current policy influence.

boundary: This record establishes national cultural judgments about perceived moral decline, government influence, and the legitimate public role of government. It does not establish objective moral change, causal policy effects, personal behavior change, political action, institutional legitimacy change, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from Gallup's published aggregate survey report; respondent microdata and local or institutional encounter records are not retained.
